subject: ULSMV MGCFA, same fit and dg

messages.author: f2b4ea1ef2b51d80
messages.subject: ULSMV MGCFA, same fit and dg
parts:
Hello,

I am fitting a MGCFA with ULMSV and ordinal data. I am using an ESEM-CFA approach, i.e. using with factor loadings from previous EFA, items are allowed to cross-load factors in the model. I am interested in testing model invariance; my attempt:

# Model 1
es_configural <- as.character(measEq.syntax(esem_model, data = df, meanstructure = T,  estimator = "ULSMV", ordered = T, return.fit = T))

# Model 2
es_thresholds <- as.character(measEq.syntax(esem_model, data = df, meanstructure = T,  estimator = "ULSMV", ordered = T,   return.fit = T, group.equal = c("thresholds")))

# Model 3
es_metric <- as.character(measEq.syntax(esem_model, data = df, meanstructure = T,  estimator = "ULSMV", ordered = T,  return.fit = T,  group.equal = c("thresholds", "loadings")))

Results show that the three models are perfectly equivalent, same df, CFI, etc. Any idea why? I had warnings (The variance-covariance matrix of the estimated parameters (vcov) does not appear to be positive definite)

Thank you very much for your help

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: ULSMV MGCFA, same fit and dg
parts:
Wu & Estabrook (2016). identification conditions change as you add more constraints. Estimates that were fixed without the added constraints become  free with the new constraints, so the changes in DF offset.

Wu, H., & Estabrook, R. (2016). Identification of confirmatory factor analysis models of different levels of invariance for ordered categorical outcomes. Psychometrika, 81(4), 1014-1045.
